explain.say: Here is a puzzle: two people can look at exactly the same thing and see two completely different stories. Look at the left side of the board. This is how you might see the new girl, Hana: she never talks and sits alone.

explain.say: From the outside you might guess she is stuck up, which means thinks she is better than others. But that is just a guess. Can you think of other reasons someone might be quiet?

explain.say: Now look at the right side: how Hana sees it. She just moved from Osaka in Japan, she is still learning English, and she is scared of getting words wrong. Does that change how you feel about her?

explain.say: This is called perspective taking, which means trying to see from someone else's side. Watch Lucas: he wonders why Hana is quiet. Instead of guessing, what could he do?

faq.q: How can I see things from someone else's side?
faq.a: Ask yourself three questions: What might they be feeling? What might have happened to them? What do I not know yet? Then, if you can, ask them kindly.
asks: Tell me about the How Hana sees it

faq.q: What does walk a mile in someone's shoes mean?
faq.a: It is a saying that means you cannot really judge someone until you understand their life and what they are going through.
asks: What does in their shoes mean?

faq.q: Why do people see the same thing differently?
faq.a: Because everyone has different memories, feelings, languages and cultures. Each person fills in the gaps with their own story.
asks: Tell me about the How you see it

faq.q: What if I guessed wrong about someone?
faq.a: That happens to everyone. Be friendly, get to know them, and say sorry if your guess made you unkind.

faq.q: Is seeing their side the same as agreeing?
faq.a: No. You can understand why someone feels a certain way and still disagree. Understanding just makes it easier to talk.
asks: Do I have to agree with them?

facts: Psychologists call understanding that others have different thoughts and beliefs "theory of mind"; most children start to show it around age four or five.
An onigiri is a Japanese rice ball, often wrapped in seaweed, and a common lunch for children in Japan.
